reason: The light-cone translation was developed into the single-relation light cone of lem:relation-space-tor, and the proved prop:relation-merging-barrier shows that involvement (light-cone speed 1/k per member) certifies at most (M-1)/(c-1) relations, so beyond capacity the mechanism fails. That is a proved limitation of the idea itself, and the local-generation question it served was taken over by the later pair-generation results.

The bag-gluing translation was developed into ex:relation-bag-images and thm:coordinate-relation-locality: pairs of members generate for coordinate forms whatever the hypergraph, including the triangle, which is not a tree. Treewidth is shown not to be the governing invariant, and the stronger pair-generation result supersedes the dynamic-programming route.

Closed by a one-step structural remark of the review: the degree-zero circuits give a non-local class at the lowest degree. But those circuits lift for W's clause shape (prop:degree-zero-circuits), so an expansion modulo lifting dependencies, the form the record itself adopted (conj:local-generation-modulo-dependencies), was never tried; the objection falsifies only the unmodded formulation. (Overlaps the later Kotecky-Preiss lead of the overdetermined review.)
open_statement: A3 (Tor vanishing / Taylor generation through 22k by bounded clusters; cross falls needing a shared piece)
next_attempt: Set up the polymer expansion of the Tor_1 (or Hilbert-series) correction modulo the lifting dependency classes, with groups of members sharing relations as polymers; check on the recorded chain, star, triangle and prefix-sum chain data that corrections of groups of size s start at degree about s times the onset, and test the Kotecky-Preiss criterion for W_RS densities.

reason: Developed three times: its reduction was made exact as prop:first-fall-criterion and run on the tensor and forced families, where it fails for proper-span members (ex:tensor-family-falls). The criterion now exists as a proved tool in the record; nothing further of Buchberger's reduction applies beyond what that criterion states.

Developed: Hamada's ranks were used to compute the relations among squared spans via the transversality criterion (37 = 3-rank of the line code of PG(2,9)). The current open statements do not involve ranks of squared-span relations, so its result leaves no remaining application.

No code-theoretic classification was attempted; the closure rests on the parked conj:dense-cover-generation (dependencies need no classification under it), not on a reason found by an attempt. A classification of small-weight dual codewords would list every kind of non-local dependency among few members, which bears on whether early cross falls need a shared piece.
open_statement: A3 (W_RS: early cross falls conjecturally need a shared piece; fill-point falls)
next_attempt: Use the Bagchi-Inamdar / Sorensen description of small-weight codewords of duals of point-subspace codes of PG(s,3) to classify dependencies among few members of weight up to about twice the minimum, and check whether each kind requires two members to share a linear piece.

reason: Never developed (two 'no new work' rounds); closed because value-space satisfiability puts any tensor-type dependency inside the family's own dense member, a reason tied to the parked dense-cover route. Tensor and forced families are later recorded as harmless by pinning Z, which may cover the idea, but whether every tensor-type dependency allowed by Ax-Katz has a pinnable shared part was not checked.
open_statement: A3 / A1 (whether sparse W_RS-like families carry tensor-type dependencies without a pinnable shared piece)
next_attempt: Use Chevalley-Warning/Ax-Katz to describe signed point sets with constant determinantal zero counts mod 3, and test whether each such dependency has a shared subspace of logarithmic dimension, so that prop:pinned-rank-vacuity applies.

reason: The lead's one translation, that tensor dependencies cannot lift once the base maps onto the forms' value space, was settled by the weak-base computation (clause sum nonzero on about two thirds of base points). The question it answered is decided, and no other translation was proposed.

Falsified: the coupled pair's cover by its two members has a contractible nerve (an edge), yet the union is not row-free. Nerve acyclicity therefore cannot certify generation; the failure lies in the Jordan type along the coupling, which the nerve cannot see. The algebraic Mayer-Vietoris form is the separate additivity item.

Developed over five follow-ups into end-additivity, pair directness (lem:pair-directness-range, prop:overlap-orientation); many-member additivity was then identified with cover generation between halves, i.e. a restatement of the open obstacle. Restatement of the open problem is a valid closure reason under the bar.

Developed: flat-covering sunflowers are out of budget by cor:value-space-dense-covers, and the kernel-pinning half iterated is the per-block removal with a recorded linear ceiling (renormalization bridge). Couplings, the obstruction then found, come from row sums rather than sunflowers. The spread half of the idea is carried separately by the spread-lemma lead.

Iterated pinning beyond capacity was identified as the per-block removal of the window review, whose linear ceiling is recorded. That is a supersession by a known barrier covering the whole renormalization flow, not one formulation.

Developed into lem:weak-base-anticoncentration (near uniformity below the column-spread scale) and used for the coupled pair's density; the lemma also shows that beyond capacity no uniformity statement for the full image can hold, where the obstacle now lies. The current A1 statement records that point designs cannot be found by density or spread, consistent with this closure.

Developed into prop:oriented-cylinder-repair and tested against regular coupling graphs; the orientation count is complete within the column-local framework. The value-side review then falsified pair repair for adversarial overlap graphs beyond the budget, and the dense core lies outside orientation.

Falsified as a certificate: the recorded counterexample ex:truncated-dade-special-position is free along every point of P(K') yet not free through degree 3, so support (rank-variety) data cannot certify truncated freeness; the graded Dade lemma fails in special position. Continued as the generic Jordan type lead and falsified the same way.

Used for the capacities c(b) in prop:oriented-cylinder-repair; the trivial sumset bound suffices and sharper Kneser bounds do not change which families fail. Its application (per-member capacity) is exhausted.

Falsified as a certificate: the super dimension is a pointwise ungraded invariant and the recorded truncated counterexample is non-free while free pointwise. Beyond capacity the allowed ring is not a tensor of member rings, so there is no factor-by-factor semisimplification on the dense core.

The numerical Kotecky-Preiss condition passed, but the algebraic translation was never tested. The closure says dimension-level expansions reach only the falls half (conj:fill-point-falls), which is itself still open in A3, so the idea still bears on an open statement; the coupling-distributivity argument rules out only the row-freeness half.
open_statement: A3 (W_RS randomized Taylor glue: early cross falls, fill-point falls)
next_attempt: Write the Hilbert-function correction of the allowed set ideal for W_RS as a polymer sum over connected clusters of blocks sharing pieces, and test on the recorded pair and shared-piece data that clusters without a shared piece contribute no falls below the fill point, using the passed density bound (sum of block weights at most about 1/n).

reason: Falsified as a detector: total counts factor for the coupled pair and the uncoupled control alike (prop:coupling-distributivity), so the product rule does not see couplings; level-wise counts are exactly the balance test already recorded.

Developed into conj:unit-loss-dade and prop:ideal-sum-criterion, then closed because the goal needs only no falls plus freeness over the couplings, not full value-side freeness. A graded Dade statement with margin over the smaller coupling algebra acting on the non-tensor allowed ring still seems to be what the dense core needs, and the record does not show it inapplicable there.
open_statement: A1 (dense core beyond joint capacity: freeness over the couplings of a non-tensor allowed ring)
next_attempt: State the margin form of conj:graded-dade-margin for the coupling algebra (dimension at most m-1) acting on T(E/K_0) modulo the sum of the member ideals, and test it on the three-member pure-relation configuration proposed by the dense-core return review.

reason: Superseded and falsified as a proof tool: prop:ideal-sum-criterion gives the obstruction module itself, and the value-side review shows that no bound depending only on Hilbert functions can separate free from non-free modules with equal Hilbert functions, which covers any plethystic diagnostic.

A Horace argument in T(W) was never attempted (follow-up said so), and the closure was by the same reason as the graded Dade item, namely that the value side does not reach the obstacle, a route decision rather than a reason found against the idea. Horace-type specialization is a standard method for maximal-rank and semi-regularity statements of the kind A3 conjectures.
open_statement: A3 (conj:semi-regular-relative-to-base: Tor vanishing through 22k for general or random tops)
next_attempt: Attempt a Horace-type specialization in T(W): degenerate one member span into a hyperplane and prove directness (maximal rank) of member ideals by induction on members, checking first against the (2,4,4) quadric pair defect and prop:no-horace-balancing.

reason: For general forms its content is covered by thm:generic-top-directness and subsumed by the orbit-weighted moment; for adversarial families repeated members falsify it at delta itself. Both regimes are thus settled by recorded results.

Developed into overlap orientation, multi-direction threshold and cluster flags, then closed because the obstacle lies in dense pure relations rather than sharing structure. The core translation, a subspace spread lemma reducing adversarial spans to spread ones that behave like general ones, was never located or proved, and could still reduce adversarial A1 to a random-form statement; whether that helps while the random dense core is open is unclear.
open_statement: A1 (adversarial forms: reduce the dense core to spread or random-like families)
next_attempt: Formulate a subspace spread lemma (a kernel subspace in many member spans is pinned by cor:pinned-cluster-reduction, otherwise spans are spread) with its degree cost, and test whether spread dense families satisfy the W_RS structured-class hypotheses already settled.

reason: Closed by a one-step objection (applies to random forms; A1 needs adversarial). The developed lemma lem:derivative-propagation concerns general position, and the adversarial analogue proposed by the value-side review itself, a first moment over the prefix randomness and the symmetric groups of members, was never attempted; random tops also remain within A3.
open_statement: A1 under W_RS (adversarial forms, random prefixes) and A3 (random tops)
next_attempt: Bound the orbit-weighted first moment (sum over GL(W)-orbits of the product of the two halves ideal masses on the orbit divided by its size) for random spans via the mass of member ideals on low-essential-dimension orbits, then test whether averaging over independent uniform prefixes gives an analogous moment for fixed adversarial forms.

reason: Inapplicability found: consequences of the clauses alone vanish on the allowed set, so implication chains among clauses are not falls of the row span, and chain depth does not bear on the lagged lift. The test of the lead also relied on a recalled, unread title result.

Developed in the nontrivial relation bound and relation excess entries: only relations outside the Taylor second step absorb, the seed-23 pair has none at its degree, and random pairs below the fill point have at most one. The question of the lead is answered in general, and the answer is already carried by the relation-excess conditions of A3.

Only the multiplier formulation nu = nu_0 W was tried: a multiplier fixed before the prefixes fails with high probability, and an adapted one reduces to the open adapted-design problem. Actual pseudo-calibration, truncating the low-degree moments of a planted distribution, was not attempted, and it is the standard construction for the Nullstellensatz and local designs that the certificate half of A1 now needs.
open_statement: A1 (certificate half: Nullstellensatz design, local designs on each block allowed set)
next_attempt: Define mu by pseudo-calibration against a planted model (prefixes drawn conditioned on a planted matching being allowed), truncated to low degree in the prefix randomness, and check that it kills row terms and is representable on each P_b on small boards.

reason: Developed in the junta-residue classes entry: the localization is correct, but row-sum phases carry full top-order mass without correlation, so the bound is too weak; the residue-class decomposition replaced it with sharper statements. Supersession by a stronger result after a real attempt.

Never followed up: the few-columns review is the latest entry and names this lead as its next step. It is the current A1 certificate mechanism (local designs bypassing the union), so it is live and must be queued.
open_statement: A1 (certificate half: local designs with single blocks as members)
next_attempt: For a random dense family choose the partial matching rho after the prefixes and decide whether the restricted matching design nu_rho kills every function of degree at most D supported inside one block excluded set, starting with the clause multiples aC.
